items.title: MetMalaysia warns of evening storms across peninsula, Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for parts of eight states and territories, warning residents to brace for heavy downpours, strong winds, and lightning strikes until 6:00pm today. According to the advisory issued at 3:55pm, severe convective weather is expected across several districts in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah. In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Kulim, Baling, and Sik in Kedah, alongside Jeli and Gua Musang in Kelantan.

items.title: Corporate earnings pick up, but misses still outnumber beats: CIMB Securities
items.summary: Year-on-year earnings growth was led by Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd, Westports Holdings Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd, Top Glove Corp Bhd and Genting Plantations Bhd. The firm also said consumer-sector misses, involving Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N), MyNews Holdings Bhd and 7-Eleven Malaysia Holdings Bhd, were largely due to weaker sales and higher operating expenses. Oil and gas companies, including Yinson Holdings Bhd, Petronas Chemicals and Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd, were affected by weaker-than-expected sales.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines retimes KLIA flights as airspace closes for National Day flypast rehearsals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Malaysia Airlines Bhd will retime selected flights arriving at and departing from KL International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 following temporary airspace closures in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebrations. The national airline said the temporary closures within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area are to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day Flypast 2026, resulting in scheduled aircraft take-offs and landings at KLIA being temporarily suspended during selected periods. Malaysia Airlines also reminded passengers that check-in counters close 60 minutes before scheduled departure for both domestic and international flights, while boarding gates close 30 minutes before departure.

items.title: Dutch say won't participate in 'no longer' neutral Eurovision
items.summary: THE HAGUE: The Netherlands will not participate in next year's Eurovision Song Contest, its broadcaster said Monday, saying the event can "no longer be considered neutral" given divisions over the Gaza war. "It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the Contest, undermining its neutral character. The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division," said Taco Zimmerman, Director-General of AVROTROS in a statement from the broadcaster.

items.title: Police tighten border security, urge public to avoid southern Thailand
items.summary: MELAKA: Police have stepped up security along the Malaysia-Thailand border following more than 50 bombings, arson attacks on government offices and tyre-burning incidents reported in three southern Thai provinces last Saturday. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail also urged Malaysians to avoid travelling to conflict zones in southern Thailand amid the heightened tensions. Earlier, Khalid received the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (D.G.S.M.

items.title: Ex-Sabah women and children’s hospital director sues successor, top official over removal
items.summary: Dr Yogendra Panchalingam filed the suit at the High Court of Sabah and Sarawak in Kota Kinabalu on August 21. He named Sabah Health Department deputy director Datuk Dr Abd Kahar Abd Asis and his former deputy turned successor, Dr Christine Lu Shin Yeen, as defendants. Appointed as hospital director in March 2025, Dr Yogendra denied all allegations of sexual harassment levelled against him, including complaints lodged by Dr Lu and the hospital’s corporate communications unit head, Elleyvianna Murang.

items.title: Haze worsens as 16 areas record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings nationwide rose to 16 from 10 recorded earlier this morning. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), as of 4pm today, Sarawak was the worst-hit state, with Serian recording the country's highest API reading at 192, nearing the "very unhealthy" threshold. Other areas in Sarawak that logged unhealthy air quality included Kuching (181), Samarahan (173), Sri Aman (156), Bintulu (145), and Mukah (134).

items.title: Trump's Kim gambit deepens doubts over US reliability at key moment for Asia
items.summary: DONALD Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for US security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington. The US president's abrupt decision to cut back military drills with South Korea last week, which he described as hostile to Pyongyang, has reinforced fears that Trump's unpredictability could strain alliances that have long maintained peace in the region, government officials and security experts said. Trump could also wield upcoming US military exercises with Japan in October as leverage, analysts say.

items.title: Finas to investigate allegations of cartel in film industry
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) will summon exhibitors, distributors and film producers to investigate allegations of a cartel and market dominance in the local film industry. Its chief executive officer, Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib, said that although no official complaints had been received so far, Finas was taking proactive steps to gather information and understand the situation in the industry. Meanwhile, he said Finas had received a notification from a local Tamil film producer regarding the last-minute entry of a film from India, which allegedly disrupted the producer's film screening schedule.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest hears olive‑green ‘Love And Peace’ journal altered, 64 sheets missing
items.summary: The 77th witness, forensic science lecturer and researcher from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) Dr Wan Nur Syuhaila Mat Desa, said the journals comprised a green journal marked W1, a pastel purple “Simple Style Book” journal (W2), a dark brown journal (W3) and an olive-green “Love And Peace” journal (WK9). Meanwhile, W2 contained only 53 sheets compared with 96 sheets in a new reference journal, meaning 43 sheets were missing, while W3 contained 77 sheets against 98 sheets in the reference journal, leaving 21 sheets missing. She said WK9 was received in worn and torn condition and contained only 54 sheets compared with 118 sheets in a new reference journal of the same type, meaning 64 sheets were missing.

items.title: Police tighten Malaysia–Thailand border security after Yala, Pattani, Narathiwat blasts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Police have stepped up security preparedness at the Malaysia-Thailand border following a series of explosions and attacks in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, southern Thailand, with the areas remaining under control. He said PDRM was also strengthening its prevention, early detection and rapid response approaches, as well as increasing intelligence and information sharing with Thai security agencies. Mohd Yusri said so far there were no reports of Malaysians being affected in the incident.

items.title: 57 held in Seremban raids on budget hotels linked to prostitution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers arrested 57 people in raids on three locations in Seremban believed to have been used for prostitution activities involving foreign women. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation was carried out from 2pm yesterday by officers from the Intelligence and Special Operations Division at Immigration headquarters in Putrajaya, with the cooperation of the Indonesian Embassy in Kuala Lumpur. He said the raids followed information from the embassy concerning Indonesians allegedly involved in immoral activities, followed by intelligence gathering by the department.

items.title: Khazanah deploys RM15bil under GEAR-uP initiative – Amirul Feisal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah Nasional Bhd has deployed RM15 billion to date of its RM25 billion five-year domestic investment commitment under the Finance Ministry's GEAR-uP initiative. "Of that RM120 billion, Khazanah has committed RM25 billion, and we have deployed about RM15 billion to date. Khazanah contributed the largest share at RM7.9 billion, followed by the EPF with RM5.8 billion, KWAP with RM5.4 billion and PNB with RM1.3 billion.

items.title: 120 vehicles set for 630km Pahang expedition
items.summary: A total of 120 vehicles will take part in Malayan Xpedition (MX) 2026, traversing a 630-kilometre (km) route that spans highways and challenging, unpaved logging tracks deep in the interior of Pahang. Organised by By The Billions (BTB), the expedition combines exploration, vehicle capability and environmental responsibility throughout the convoy. The technical partnerships cover equipment required to handle heavy loads and vehicle recovery situations along Pahang's challenging unpaved logging tracks.

items.title: Malaysia tightens Thai border security after southern attacks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have stepped up security preparedness along the Malaysia-Thailand border following a series of explosions and attacks in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, with the situation remaining under control. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the measures included deploying personnel from the Southeast and Northern Brigades of the General Operations Force (GOF), as well as intensifying patrols along the border fencing, Sungai Golok and routes that could potentially be used for infiltration. He said the police was also strengthening prevention, early detection and rapid response measures, while increasing intelligence and information sharing with Thai security agencies.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia to synchronise haze suppression ops as monsoon and El Niño converge
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to ramp up preventive measures to tackle cross-border haze, to safeguard air quality, especially in the lead-up to the National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the commitment was reached during a phone call today with his Indonesian counterpart, Environment Minister Jumhur Hidayat. The 69th National Day celebration is set to take place at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31, while the Malaysia Day celebration will be held in Kuching, Sarawak, on Sept 16.

items.title: Iran warns vessels violating Hormuz transit rules of fines, detention
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran has issued a warning that vessels violating its arrangements for transiting the Strait of Hormuz could face restrictions, including fines, detention, or confiscation, the Persian Gulf Strait Authority wrote in a post on X. The PGSA, a new body Iran has established with the aim of managing the strait, has said cargo owners should refer to an updated list of vessels deemed non-compliant for voyages relating to the Persian Gulf. Vessels engaging in operations including ship-to-ship transfers or transshipment with non-compliant vessels will also be added to the restricted list, it said.

items.title: Finas moves to combat ‘cartels’ and ensure fair competition in local film market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) is moving to convene industry players to address alleged distribution monopolies and ensure fair competition within the local cinematic market. Chief executive officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib acknowledged growing anxiety over the concentration of control in film distribution, specifically where a single entity dominates production, funding, and distribution. We want fair trade and opportunities for all industry players,” Azmir told reporters at the new Menara Finas headquarters in Damansara Damai.

items.title: Economy minister: Tabung Haji’s RM96b investments make governance crucial to market confidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — The government has cast the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) findings on Tabung Haji’s management between 2014 and 2020 as part of a wider push to tighten governance, strengthen accountability and restore public confidence in national institutions. From an economic perspective, he noted, Tabung Haji’s governance is crucial given its scale and role. “With investments exceeding RM96 billion, Tabung Haji’s governance has wider implications for confidence in institutions and the domestic market.

items.title: Southeast Asia's budget airlines eye recovery but fuel scars linger
items.summary: HONG KONG: Southeast Asia's budget carriers are hoping the worst of the Middle East-driven fuel shock is behind them but face a difficult second half as margins remain under pressure and strained household budgets threaten demand, airline executives and analysts said. The latest quarterly results from Malaysia's AirAsia, Singapore Airlines' budget arm Scoot and the Philippines' Cebu Pacific showed that efforts to recoup soaring fuel costs through higher fares fell short. AirAsia and Cebu Pacific reported net losses, while Scoot's operating loss nearly doubled.

items.title: Mara takes first step towards setting up its own hospital
items.summary: He said Mara already had a comprehensive healthcare ecosystem to support the hospital, including 160 U.n.i KLINIK, U.n.i Farmasi and U.n.i Dental outlets, as well as institutions producing medical and healthcare professionals. "Mara has a complete ecosystem for a hospital, with 160 U.n.i KLINIK, U.n.i Farmasi and U.n.i Dental outlets, UniKL Royal College of Medicine Perak (RCMP) producing doctors and Kolej Poly-Tech Mara (KPTM) training nurses," he said in a Facebook post today. "Hospital Mara could even serve as a living laboratory for Mara students and researchers.

items.title: KTMB rolls out special timetable, adds trains for northern routes during school holidays and Merdeka
items.summary: It added that the move would increase the total number of services on the Butterworth-Padang Besar-Butterworth route from 38 to 46 services per day. “Of the total, four additional services will be provided for the Padang Besar-Butterworth route, taking the total to 23 services per day compared with 19 services under the regular timetable. “Four additional services will also be provided for the Butterworth-Padang Besar route, bringing the total to 23 services per day,” it added.

items.title: Bank Negara approved MNRB's acquisition of Labuan Re
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MNRB Holdings Bhd has secured Bank Negara Malaysia's approval to acquire an 80 per cent stake in Labuan Reinsurance (L) Ltd (Labuan Re) for US$100.69 million (RM400.49 million), bringing the proposed deal closer to completion. Upon completion, MNRB will hold 80 per cent of Labuan Re directly, while its unit Malaysian Reinsurance Bhd (Malaysian Re) will retain its existing 20 per cent stake, making Labuan Re a wholly-owned subsidiary of MNRB. The vendors comprise CIMB Bank Bhd, Hicom Holdings Bhd, MISC Bhd, Petroliam Nasional Bhd, Telekom Malaysia Bhd, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, Lembaga Tabung Angkatan Tentera, Malayan Banking Bhd, Public Bank Bhd and RHB Bank Bhd.

items.title: Forensic analysis links 15 loose pages to Zara Qairina's journal, inquest told
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: There is strong scientific support for the conclusion that 15 loose pages examined in the inquest into Zara Qairina Mahathir's death originally came from a "Love and Peace" journal labelled WK9, the Coroner's Court heard today. Forensic science lecturer and researcher Dr Dzulkiflee Ismail said the finding was based on chemical analysis of the 15 loose pages, marked Y1 to Y15, and the WK9 journal. Dzulkiflee said the papers underwent chemical analysis using Attenuated Total Reflectance-Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy, combined with chemometric techniques.

items.title: Asteel gets RM18mil takeover offer from Clifford Hii
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asteel Group Bhd says it has received an RM18 million takeover offer from businessman Clifford Hii. Under Malaysia's takeover rules, Hii is required to make a mandatory offer for the remaining shares held by Asteel's minority shareholders. Despite seeking control of the company, Hii does not intend to privatise Asteel and plans to maintain its listing.

items.title: Tahfiz teacher in Ampang pleads not guilty to four sexual assault charges on pupils
items.summary: The accused, Muhammad Ilyas Jamaludin, is alleged to have committed the offences against the two boys, aged 10 and 11, at the premises between July and August 2026. The charges were preferred under Sections 14(a) and 14(b) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, and read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act. Under Section 14(a) and 14(b), the offence carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment and caning and Section 16(1) provides for an additional term of up to five years’ imprisonment and no fewer than two strokes of the cane, upon conviction.

items.title: PetDagang's Q2 earnings soar 46pct to RM387mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Dagangan Bhd's (PetDagang) net profit jumped 46 per cent to RM387 million in the second quarter of financial year 2026 (Q2 FY26) from RM265.5 million a year earlier. Its net profit rose to RM387 million from RM265.5 million a year earlier, while revenue surged 77 per cent to RM16 billion from RM9 billion previously due to higher average selling prices. For the first half of FY26, PetDagang's net profit rose 20 per cent to RM670 million from RM559 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 50 per cent to RM27 billion from RM18 billion previously.

items.title: Thai man pleads not guilty to possessing 6,000 yaba pills in Kelantan
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A 45-year-old Thai man pleaded not guilty at the magistrates' court here today to possessing 6,000 yaba pills in Rantau Panjang. Saliki Deraman entered the plea after the charge was read before Magistrate Syed Farid Syed Ali. Saliki was also charged under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for entering Malaysia without a travel document.

items.title: Adults aged 31-59 make up bulk of drug abuse cases
items.summary: KUALA BERANG: People aged 31 to 59 recorded the highest number of drug abuse cases in the country, with 92,590 individuals or 71.1 per cent of the total recorded from January to June this year, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh. He said 34,471 people aged 15 to 30, or 26.5 per cent, were recorded during the same period, while 3,229 people aged 60 and above accounted for 2.5 per cent. Ruslin said the statistics showed that drug abuse continued to affect various age groups, including individuals aged up to 63.

items.title: IGP urges Malaysians to reduce travel to southern Thailand amid tense security
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 24 — Police have stepped up security along the Malaysia-Thailand border following more than 50 bombings, arson attacks on local government offices and tyre-burning reported in three provinces of southern Thailand last Saturday. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail also urged the public to stay away from the conflict zones, citing safety concerns amid the escalating tension. Earlier at the ceremony, Mohd Khalid received the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (D.G.S.M.)

items.title: E&O's Q1 net profit surges to RM58.1mil on higher revenue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eastern & Oriental Bhd's net profit rose 27.9 per cent to RM58.11 million in the first quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM45.42 million a year ago, driven by higher revenue. The property developer's quarterly revenue climbed 53.4 per cent to RM281.47 million from RM183.51 million previously. In Q1 FY27, E&O's property sales more than doubled to RM356.0 million from RM153.0 million in the previous corresponding quarter, reflecting sustained demand for the group's ongoing developments.

items.title: Madrasah instructor charged with sexually assaulting two young brothers
items.summary: MUAR: A madrasah instructor was charged in the Sessions Court here today with four counts of sexually assaulting two brothers, aged 10 and 11, at a madrasah hostel in Batu Pahat last month. Muhammad Hilmi Mohamad Noor, 24, pleaded not guilty to all charges before Sessions Court judge Emelia Kaswati Mohamad Khalid. However, the court granted bail of RM15,000 for all four charges.

items.title: 'Gapai' brings Merdeka spirit to life through generations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The spirit of Merdeka comes to life in "Gapai", a three-minute film launched by Permodalan Nasional Bhd's Merdeka Ventures today. PNB Merdeka Ventures chief executive officer Datuk Dr Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim said the film also reflected the history and community surrounding the Merdeka 118 precinct, which stands on the site where independence was declared. Meanwhile, as part of its Merdeka month celebrations, the Merdeka 118 precinct is collaborating with Locco to host a three-day celebration from Aug 29 to 31 at Stadium Merdeka and Merdeka Boulevard.

items.title: #NSTViral: Rohingya family making a 'home' of public spaces in Larkin
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A six-member Rohingya family has been living rough at various public places in Larkin here for more than two months. A resident in the area said the family had moved between several locations, including a playground, shop lot pavements and the vicinity of a surau. The resident urged the authorities to locate the family and take appropriate action.

items.title: Employers raise concerns over proposed RM3,100 minimum wage [WATCH]
items.summary: He said a "living wage" benchmark and a "legal minimum wage" were distinct concepts. A living wage is aimed at meeting basic living costs, while the legal minimum wage is the lowest pay required by law. Malaysia's statutory minimum wage currently stands at RM1,700.

items.title: Malaysia ready to help Indonesia tackle forest fires, haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is ready to assist Indonesia, if requested, particularly in efforts to quickly put out forest and land fires, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup. He said the offer was made in the spirit of good neighbourliness and Asean solidarity following a telephone call today with Indonesian Environment Minister Jumhur Hidayat to discuss hot weather, the El Nino phenomenon and transboundary haze affecting the region. He said Malaysia appreciated and supported the swift action taken by the Indonesian government under President Prabowo Subianto to intensify efforts to combat forest and land fires.

items.title: KTMB adds eight KTM Komuter Utara train services for holidays, National Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) will operate eight additional KTM Komuter Utara services on the Butterworth-Padang Besar route from Thursday until Monday (Aug 27 to 31) for the school holidays and National Day celebrations. The move will increase total daily services on the Butterworth-Padang Besar-Butterworth route from 38 to 46. Four additional services will also run on the Butterworth-Padang Besar route, bringing its daily total to 23.

items.title: Key WISE expressway project in Perak secures RM5.55bil funding
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR: Funding amounting to RM5.55 billion for the West Ipoh Span Expressway (WISE) has been secured, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said. They said that they have already secured funding from Hong Leong Bank. Saarani said the funding issue had been resolved and the sukuk issued, allowing the 60km project to proceed.

items.title: Sabah Electricity confirms fatal electrocution during pole replacement works in Sandakan, one injured
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 24 — A worker was electrocuted during installation works on an electric pole at Bandar Tabin Jaya, here on Saturday. “Personnel from the Sabah Electricity helped disconnect the electricity before the man was brought down using special equipment,” he said in a statement. Meanwhile, Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd (Sabah Electricity) has confirmed the incident involving two contractor workers during electrical pole replacement works near the traffic light junction leading to Taman Mawar here, on Aug 22.

items.title: Three Indonesians plead guilty to smuggling three tonnes of untaxed tin
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Three Indonesian men pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court today to attempting to smuggle three tonnes of untaxed tin ingots and powder earlier this month. The accused, Zulkifli, 46, Suhaimi, 30, and Basri, 45, entered their pleas before magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman. They were jointly charged with transporting and transferring 121 packages containing 3,000kg of untaxed tin ingots and powder.

items.title: MSM Malaysia swings back to profit on Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MSM Malaysia Holdings Bhd returned to the black with a net profit of RM23.43 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q2 FY26), compared to a net loss of RM29.74 million a year ago. The refined sugar producer said the net profit was attributable to higher margins and lower other operating expenses. For the first half of FY26, MSM recorded a net profit of RM4.58 million, compared to a net loss of RM26.02 million a year ago.

items.title: Twins make history with top honours at engineering awards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Identical twins Dr Serene Lock Sow Mun and Irene Lock Sow Mei, 36, achieved national recognition after being named among Malaysia's top engineers at the Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM) Engineering Awards last night. Serene, an associate professor at Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP), became the first woman to win the National Young Engineer Award, while her sister Irene, a senior process engineer at Petronas, received the Special Mention International Engineering Award (SMIEA) 2026. This recognition motivates me to contribute even more to the engineering field," Irene said.

items.title: Roller coaster mishap at Subang Jaya theme park leaves ten hurt, police investigating
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 24 — Ten people sustained minor injuries in a roller coaster incident at a theme park here. District police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said the incident took place at about 9pm on Saturday, while the report was lodged with police at 11.45am yesterday. “Anyone with information can contact the Subang Jaya Police headquarters at 03-78627100,” he said.

items.title: PM Anwar to deliver National Day ‘Amanat Perdana’ at Dataran Merdeka
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will deliver the 2026 National Day ‘Amanat Perdana’ on Aug 30 to convey the aspirations and hopes of the Madani Government leadership on the importance of embracing the spirit of independence and fostering patriotism among Malaysians. Organised by the National Unity Ministry, the event will be held at Dataran Merdeka, with various programmes starting as early as 5pm, including the Merdeka Eve Animation Concert, World Festival of Lights, Gema Perpaduan Malaysia Madani cultural performance, a special Independence Musical segment and performances by leading local artistes. National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the well-being that the country aspires to enjoy could not be achieved without strong unity.

items.title: Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek among top honourees at Melaka’s state awards
items.summary: Fadhlina received the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (D.G.S.M) which carries the title of Datuk Seri. Also receiving the same title were Chief Justice of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail and Chief Commissioner of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. Meanwhile, 56 individuals received the Darjah Cemerlang Seri Melaka (D.C.S.M) award which carries the title of Datuk Wira, including Benut assemblyman Datuk Mohd Sumali Reduan, Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar, National Solid Waste Management Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azhar Abd Hamid and Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar.

items.title: Linkedua shutdown: Eight including motoring influencer held after staging illegal race on Malaysia-Singapore link
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 24 — A motoring influencer was among eight local men remanded for four days to assist investigations into a case involving the closure of a section of the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (Linkedua) to stage an illegal race last Saturday. The remand order, effective today until Thursday (Aug 27), was issued by Magistrate R. Salini after police applied for the order at the Kulai Magistrate’s Court to assist investigations under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act (RTA) 1987. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad was reported to have said that the group was believed to have blocked the road from KM33 at the Senai Utara Toll interchange to KM31 at the Johor Premium Outlet (JPO) interchange on Linkedua to stage an illegal race.

items.title: Penang land sale probe: MACC extends remand for agency chief and company director
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 24 — The remand period for a government agency chairman and a company director has been extended for another three days until Wednesday to assist investigations into an abuse of power case involving the disposal of land in Penang, with losses estimated at RM1.96 million. On Thursday, five people, comprising a government agency chairman, two company directors, a technical manager and a female clerk, were detained at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office. The chairman is suspected of abusing his position while serving as deputy chairman and a member of the Board of Directors to approve the sale of eight plots of land belonging to an agency under a ministry in Seberang Perai Selatan in 2015.

items.title: FMM dismisses MTUC’s RM3,100 minimum wage proposal as unrealistic for businesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) has rejected a proposal by the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) to raise the national minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM3,100, cautioning that an 82.4 per cent surge is detached from prevailing economic realities. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said that while the federation supports higher wages as Malaysia strives for high-income status, an abrupt RM1,400 increase in a single revision remains unprecedented. Under the National Wages Consultative Council (NWCC) Act, the next mandatory statutory wage review is slated for February 2027.

items.title: E-hailing driver charged with attempted murder after setting woman on fire in Kepong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — An e-hailing driver has claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to an attempted murder charge after allegedly dousing a 62-year-old woman in petrol and setting her ablaze in Kepong earlier this month. Ang Kam Tong, 58, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before Judge Surita Budin, FMT reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shakila Shariff objected to bail, telling the court that Ang had attempted to evade arrest.

items.title: Court of Appeal dismisses Indira Gandhi’s RM100m suit despite flagging police shortcomings
items.summary: While dismissing the appeal, a three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan highlighted material deficiencies in police records concerning efforts to execute an arrest warrant against her fugitive former husband, K. Pathmanathan, also known as Muhammad Riduan Abdullah, NST reported. Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid also sat on the bench. Delivering the unanimous decision, Faizah ruled that the available evidence failed to establish that any specific police omission directly prevented Pathmanathan’s arrest or the recovery of Prasana.

items.title: Sarawak leads haze misery as Serian hits 194, unhealthy API spreads to Selangor, Kedah, Penang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Ten areas in four states recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian, Sarawak recording the highest reading, nearing the very unhealthy level. Other areas in the state that recorded unhealthy air quality were Kuching (176), Samarahan (172), Sri Aman (158) and Bintulu (125). A further 58 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: Three squatter homes razed in Sentul blaze, 26‑year‑old man treated for burn injuries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A man suffered burns to his body and legs in a fire that destroyed three squatter houses in Jalan Ismail Ghani, Kampung Kasipillay, Sentul, here early this morning. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar said the emergency call was received at 1.15am before teams from Sentul, Hang Tuah and Gombak Selatan Fire and Rescue Stations rushed to the location. “Upon arrival of the fire brigade at the location, the fire was found to involve three semi-permanent squatter houses with a total area of 4,872 square feet.

items.title: Melaka polls: Anwar, Amirudin meet as Pakatan weighs BN pact
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met with Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari over the weekend, with a potential electoral pact with Barisan Nasional for the next Melaka state polls believed to be high on the agenda. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil confirmed the meeting took place, though he noted he was not briefed on the specifics. On the BN front, chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has maintained that the coalition will not enter any automatic arrangement with Perikatan, leaving the ultimate decision to Melaka Chief Minister and state Umno-Barisan chief Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

items.title: Noise row in Sarawak turns violent as knife attack leaves man wounded outside Bau home
items.summary: Bau District police chief Supt Mohd Haide A. Rahman said the incident took place at around 1pm, when the complainant became involved in a heated argument with the suspect. “The victim also sustained a minor laceration to his left wrist while attempting to block the knife during the assault,” he said in a statement. Mohd Haide said the suspect had been identified and the knife had been seized.

items.title: Melaka election countdown? Perikatan hints at polls within two months
items.summary: AYER KEROH, Aug 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has teased a tight timeline for the Melaka state election, suggesting the polls could be held in less than two months and putting the coalition’s election machinery on high alert. PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar warned that a 60-day window should not be mistaken for a long period, but rather viewed as a critical countdown to determine who will govern the state, NST reported. Speaking in the presence of PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, Ahmad Samsuri, who also serves as a PAS vice-president, vowed that PN is prepared to govern Melaka regardless of the political landscape.

items.title: Mr Opposition — The legacy of Tan Chee Khoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A steady crowd of 150 or so were present at yesterday’s public forum marking 30 years since the death of former opposition leader Dr Tan Chee Khoon. Jointly organised by Aliran and his youngest daughter Tan Poh Lai, the event at the KLSCAH is one of three subtitled Merdeka, Multiracialism and Dissent, Without Fear or Favour. He was elected to Parliament in 1964 under the Labour Party, 1969 under Gerakan and 1974 under Pekemas.

items.title: Hadi: Perikatan and BN already in talks for Melaka state election pact
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) have entered negotiations to forge a cooperation pact for the upcoming Melaka state election (PRN). PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang disclosed that talks between representatives appointed by the central leadership of both coalitions kicked off three days ago, Sinar Harian reported. While acknowledging that discussions are in their infancy, Abdul Hadi noted that the initial momentum has been promising.

items.title: Housewife in her 70s tricked by ritual scam in Sibu, police confirm RM317,000 losses
items.summary: Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the local woman, in her 70s, lodged a police report yesterday over the incident, which occurred on July 19 in the Sibu Market area. He said the victim was initially approached by an unidentified woman, believed to be a Chinese national based on her accent, who asked for directions to a Chinese traditional medicine shop, allegedly to obtain medicine for her mother-in-law. Abang Zainal Abidin said the suspects then offered a protection ritual and asked the victim to hand over cash and jewellery for the purpose.

items.title: Amirudin says viral Sukma holiday poster fake, official decision based on medal tally tonight
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 24 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has denied the authenticity of a viral poster announcing a special public holiday to mark the state’s victory at the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma). Please take note and remain patient,” he said. Yesterday, state Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi was reported as saying that the state government would consider declaring a special public holiday if the Selangor contingent emerged as the overall champion at the Games.

items.title: Record-breaking crowds storm Menara Merdeka 118 for IHH Sky Race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, August 24 — More than 8,000 athletes stormed the 118 floors of Menara Merdeka 118 over the weekend, as the IHH Sky Race returned for its second year to cement its status as Malaysia’s premier tower running event. Japanese tower runner Ryoji Watanabe claimed victory with a blistering time of 15 minutes and 38 seconds. Soh secured second place, conquering the 2,845 steps in 15 minutes and 48 seconds, while Australian Mark Bourne followed in third at 16 minutes and 33 seconds.
